The Optimality Check of the Coefficients That a Kinked Penalty Sets to Zero

Source: R/inference.R
zero_readings.Rd

Computes the largest ratio \(|s_j|/\kappa_j\) over the coefficients that a penalty with a kink sets exactly to zero, where \(s_j\) is the derivative of the log-likelihood in that coefficient and \(\kappa_j\) is the size of the kink there.

Usage

zero_readings(spec, design, obj, coef, hyper, lab)

Arguments

spec, design, obj, coef, hyper

The fit's specification, design, objective, coefficients and hyperparameters.

lab

coef_labels() of the design.

Value

NULL where no coefficient at zero has a finite ratio, otherwise a named vector with ratio and n, the number of coefficients at zero.

Details

At a zero the penalty has no derivative, and the condition for an optimum is not a vanishing gradient but \(|s_j| \le \kappa_j\): the pull of the likelihood must not exceed what the kink holds back. A ratio at or below one therefore means that every zero is where it belongs, and a ratio above one identifies a coefficient that would improve the objective by leaving zero. The standard error does not enter, because a coefficient at zero has none.

With the other coefficients fixed and a kink proportional to \(\lambda\), the coefficient with the largest ratio \(r < 1\) leaves zero at a \(\lambda\) that is the fraction \(r\) of the fitted one, while along a path the other coefficients move and the threshold moves with them. The ratio is not a test of significance, and values close to one are ordinary where \(\lambda\) was chosen on a grid, because the next coefficient to enter is close to its threshold by construction.

The kink is read from the penalty's own gradient just to the right of zero, so it is \(\lambda\) for a lasso, \(\lambda\alpha\) for an elastic net and \(\lambda\) scaled by the spread under standardize, with no formula per family. The penalties are separable, so every zero is moved off in one evaluation.

See also

statmod_certificate(), certificate_readings()
